newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to take Australia salmon dispute to WTO.
newsitem.headline: Canada to take Australia salmon dispute to WTO.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Wednesday it wanted the World Trade Organisation to settle a dispute over Australia's ban on imports of uncooked salmon.
Canada's International Trade Minister Art Eggleton and Fisheries Minister Fred Mifflin said they would request a dispute settlement panel on March 20.

"We think there's no justification for the banning of ... our uncooked salmon from their country," Eggleton told reporters. "We don't think there have been health reasons to do it, so we're taking them to the WTO."
The Australian government said last December that it would maintain its ban on uncooked salmon products despite years of consultations on the issue.
Eggleton invited the Australian government to resolve the dispute before the World Trade Organisation got involved, but he did not hold out much hope.

"For some period of time we have tried to bring about a resolution to the matter, but there's been a continuing stall," Eggleton said. "There's always an opportunity to reach a settlement, even after the process is under way. But we haven't been able to do that for a long period of time. This has been a dispute going on for about 20 years."
In 1975, Australia introduced a quarantine measure banning the import of fresh salmon products, requiring all imported salmon to be either heat-treated or canned, the Canadian government said.
